title: Act, Confirm, or Stop? Smarter behavior for AI assistants, wearables & robots — Amit Desai, Roku
talk_summary: Amit Desai argues that beyond improving raw accuracy, systems should add explicit 'stop' and 'confirm' behaviors under uncertainty, choosing thresholds by minimizing a user-outcome cost function (weighted by relative badness of wrong-act vs. stop vs. confirm). He shows on a toy smart-speaker example that optimizing two thresholds cuts expected user cost from 2.1 to ~1.26 'ouch points' per turn without changing accuracy.

takeaways.technique: Cost-weighted act/confirm/stop thresholds for agent actions
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of a single confidence cutoff, they define a user-outcome cost function assigning different penalties to wrong-act, stop, and confirm outcomes, then optimize thresholds to minimize expected cost rather than guessing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we've basically turned this into a problem of minimizing a cost function. It's a user cost function
takeaways.numbers: 2.1 -> 1.9 (naive 65% threshold) -> 1.27 (optimized single threshold) -> 1.26 (two thresholds with confirm)

takeaways.technique: Asymmetric penalties for false-accept vs false-reject
takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly quantify that a wrong action is much worse than a stop/ask, and weight the decision accordingly rather than treating both errors equally.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The bad outcomes are not equally bad. They're not the same thing from a user perspective.
takeaways.numbers: wrong-act unit cost 10s vs stop 4s vs confirm-yes 2s vs confirm-no 6s

takeaways.technique: Calibrated confidence + offline threshold optimization on labeled data
takeaways.what_they_do: They annotate ~1000 examples, attach a calibrated confidence score, plot distributions, and sweep thresholds to find the cost-minimizing operating point rather than eyeballing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if we just took a guesstimate we would end up with a worse situation than a more rigorous approach

takeaways.what_they_do: Adds a middle 'confirm' behavior between acting and stopping, splitting the confidence distribution into three regions with two thresholds.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have a third obviously um option which is to confirm
takeaways.numbers: confirm layer improved 1.27 -> 1.26 in their toy case (marginal)
